mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the prediction is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to reduced risk-free discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when Fed Funds > 4% in prior month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 3.5% for two consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as labor market tightening supports stronger corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with UNRATE > 3.5 trend (Pearson r < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly HOUST (household spending index) exceeds 1430 for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive, reflecting pent-up consumer demand.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite the three-month HOUST > 1430 streak (95% CI does not include zero).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) below 105 for two consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, predicting a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1) during INDPRO contraction periods.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL by at least 0.25 percentage points each are required to trigger a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return, reflecting dual disinflation.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < prev and CPIAUCSL < prev by ≥0.25% in the same month, for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when both triggers are met (IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in PAYEMS (employment months) below 150,000 in a month, followed by a rise above 155,000 the next month, predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return due to labor market uncertainty.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 150,000 then PAYEMS > 155,000 in the following month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such PAYEMS regime (IC > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (GDP chained) grows at an annualized rate above 4% over the prior quarter, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive, reflecting optimism about economic momentum.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns show no correlation with GDPC1 >4% growth (Spearman's rho < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in RSAFS (retail sales) below 700,000 million dollars predicts a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as weak retail sales signal consumer weakness.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative during RSAFS contraction (95% CI includes zero).
